answer: Every anchor chain leaves the foundry with its links counted and stamped, and the length is filed with the harbour master before the chain may be sold. A ocean chain bought from a scrap dealer fails the count: the karst of the harbour must hold chains the foundry stamped, and a scrap chain rusts through in a season. Forging the chain means running a foundry for a month, casting 400 links and paying 19,200, while the ember stamp on each link is read at every anchoring, so a chain whose links were never counted drags its ship onto the rocks.
